questions.prompt: The biggest security reason to use `prepare()`/`execute()` with placeholders is:
options: The user's data is sent as parameters and never becomes part of the SQL string — preventing SQL injection
questions.explain: **Prepared statements separate code from data** — the injection string is never executed as SQL.

questions.prompt: Which PDO option set is the course's standard?
questions.explain: The three sacred options: **ERRMODE_EXCEPTION, FETCH_ASSOC, EMULATE_PREPARES=false**.

questions.prompt: After an INSERT and an UPDATE respectively, which calls report the new id and the number of changed rows?
questions.explain: **lastInsertId() lives on the PDO connection; rowCount() on the statement.** (mysql2/Node equivalent: r.insertId / r.affectedRows.)

questions.prompt: Why does the course mandate `utf8mb4` instead of MySQL's `utf8`?
options: MySQL's utf8 is broken 3-byte encoding — utf8mb4 is real 4-byte Unicode (emoji, all scripts)
questions.explain: MySQL's legacy `utf8` stores max **3 bytes** per character — it can't hold emoji/astral-plane chars. **utf8mb4** is the real thing; use it for every table + the DSN charset.

questions.prompt: A transfer debits one account and credits another. The guarantee transactions give is:
options: All-or-nothing: commit() makes both permanent; any exception → rollBack() undoes both
Speed: both updates run in parallel
questions.explain: **Atomicity** — beginTransaction → updates → commit, with rollBack in the catch. Requires the InnoDB engine (transactional/ACID), which is why every course table uses it.

questions.prompt: With real prepared statements (EMULATE_PREPARES=false), reusing a named placeholder twice raises SQLSTATE ______ (5 chars).
questions.explain: **HY093** — invalid parameter number. Fix: unique names per occurrence (`:q_title`, `:q_author`).

questions.prompt: Which engine + why does every course table use it?
options: InnoDB — transactional ACID engine (transactions, row locks, foreign keys)
questions.explain: **ENGINE=InnoDB** — ACID transactions (beginTransaction/commit/rollBack literally don't work on MyISAM), row-level locking, FK constraints.
